Cold blue-gray haze gathers around an isolated, irregular mass of dark rock. From it rises a vast, brooding Gothic cathedral complex, weathered brown-gray masonry and dark slate roofs cut by deep unlit window openings and strong angular shadows.

One enormous central structure crowds the heart of the scene: connected cathedral halls, steep gabled roofs, massive rectangular blocks, flying buttresses, arcaded façades, and a dense forest of tall needle-like spires and open belfry towers. Around its perimeter, several smaller but still monumental chapel, gatehouse, and tower clusters stand across deep rocky chasms. Long elevated stone bridges and narrow causeways tie them back to the core. Wings and bridges radiate outward in an asymmetrical, organic footprint rather than following a clean grid. The central architecture is extremely dense; broad gaps of empty, mist-covered terrain separate the outer structures.

Beneath the walkways lie rough stepped cliffs, oversized boulders, narrow gullies, and dark uneven ground. Scattered pale rocks mark a broken outer edge before it dissolves into fog. At street level, elevated pedestrian terraces meet carved stone balustrades, rows of pointed arches, and repeated recessed wall panels. Tall supporting piers flare into buttress-like feet over the ravine.

Only sparse secondary details remain: small finials along parapets, decorative tracery, occasional roof ornaments. Widely spaced warm orange lamps on bridge posts and entrances provide a restrained glow against the cool, dim, misty atmosphere.
